explanations: There is no defect. Each module has one cohesive job: parseReading validates input, ThresholdEvaluator only decides and publishes alerts, and TelemetryIngestService orchestrates. Dependencies point at the narrow interfaces in ports.ts (ReadingStore, RuleSource, AlertPublisher) rather than concrete databases or brokers, and breaches() is a pure function that can be tested alone. Depending on the concrete ThresholdEvaluator class looks like tight coupling, but it is an in-process domain component with its own injected ports, so it can be constructed with fakes in tests.

ThresholdEvaluator depends only on the RuleSource interface (rulesFor), so a new implementation plugged in at construction is enough. The ingest service never touches rules, parseReading is unrelated to rules, and the interface itself does not need to change.

Each item is parsed in its own try/catch; InvalidReadingError increments rejected and the loop continues. The 3 accepted readings are appended and evaluated. Only non-validation errors are rethrown, and invalid items are never stored.

breaches() uses strict comparisons: value > rule.above and value < rule.below. 80 > 80 is false and 80 < 10 is false, so it returns false. Neither bound is inclusive, and a matching metric is still required by evaluate().
